summary.title: Creating filter.py to strip JavaScript from HTML
summary.body: I've created `filter.py`. Run it as `python3 filter.py file.html`; it removes JavaScript from the file and saves the result in place. **Testing:** I checked about 45 known XSS tricks, and in each case the dangerous part was removed. A clean sample page with tables, headers, comments, inline CSS, forms, an inline SVG drawing and non-English characters came back byte-for-byte unchanged. Running it on 20,000 random inputs caused no crashes, and running it twice never changed the result further. I haven't loaded any output in a real browser to confirm that no script runs. **How it works:** the script reads the HTML the same way a browser does. Anything that isn't dangerous is copied over exactly, so spacing, quoting, character codes like `&`, comments and line endings stay the same. It leaves the file alone if nothing needs removing. **What it removes:** - **Script blocks:** `` tags. - **Plugin tags:** `
